content_units: Best Fit for Graduate Data Analysis

Your priorities rank as:   portability first  ,   battery life second  ,   enough long-term performance third  . On that basis, the best overall pick is   A  , with   B   as the power-heavy alternative and   C   as the budget trade-off.
Laptop Ranking for Your Use Case
Rank   Option   Price   Weight   Battery   Memory/Storage   Best For   Main Trade-off
1     A       USD 1,249       1.24 kg       18 hr     16GB / 512GB   Best balance for travel + all-day school use   Less RAM/storage headroom than B
2     B       USD 1,199     1.55 kg   10 hr     32GB / 1TB     Best future-proofing for heavier notebooks and multitasking   Noticeably heavier, much shorter battery
3     C       USD 999     1.75 kg   8 hr   16GB / 512GB   Lowest price   Least portable and weakest battery for frequent travel
Why this ranking fits your priorities
-   Option A wins   because it is the lightest by a clear margin and has by far the best battery life.
- For   browser tabs, Python notebooks, light SQL, and video calls  ,   16GB RAM is still sufficient today   for most graduate workflows.
- Since you travel   twice a month  , the combination of   1.24 kg + 18-hour battery   matters every single trip.
-   Option B   is the better machine if you expect:
- larger datasets in memory
- heavier multitasking
- Docker/VM use
- more advanced analytics tools over time
But it gives up too much on your top two priorities.
-   Option C   is the value pick, but it is the least aligned with what you care about most. It is bigger, heavier, and has the shortest battery life of the three.
Top Picks in Card View
Option 1:   A — Best overall for your priorities     Lightest and longest-lasting; strong enough for graduate analytics work if your tasks stay moderate     Best travel companion
- Best match for commuting, campus use, flights, and library days
- 16GB RAM should handle Jupyter, many tabs, SQL tools, and calls comfortably
- Best chance of feeling effortless to carry for 4 years
Option 2:   B — Best for long-term performance headroom     32GB RAM and 1TB SSD give the most breathing room for future workloads     Best future-proof specs
- Strongest choice if you expect bigger notebooks or memory-hungry workflows
- Better if “avoid slowdowns over 4 years” matters more than weight and battery
- Still under budget, which makes it a serious alternative
Option 3:   C — Best if budget savings matter most     Gets the job done for common student tasks at the lowest price     Best upfront value
- Fine for lighter workloads
- More likely to feel bulky during frequent travel
- Least appealing if battery life is important
Buying Decision Guidance
Choose   A   if you want:
- the easiest laptop to carry
- the best unplugged endurance
- a machine that feels best for travel and campus mobility
Choose   B   if you want:
- maximum protection against future slowdown
- more RAM for heavier notebooks and multitasking
- more storage so you do not think about space for a long time
Skip   C   unless:
- saving   USD 200–250   matters more than portability and battery
- you are comfortable with a larger, heavier device on trips
Final Recommendation
Recommended winner: A

It is the best fit for the priorities you stated in the order you stated them. It gives you the strongest combination of   low weight  ,   excellent battery life  , and   adequate performance   for graduate-level data analysis work.
Trade-off alternative: B

If your meaning of “avoid slowdowns over the next 4 years” is more important than portability, then   B   is the smarter long-term buy. Its   32GB RAM and 1TB SSD   give it the best technical runway, and it still fits under your budget cap.
